name: ACCESS_COPY
doc: These constants specify the access mode for a memory mapping. ACCESS_READ provides read-only access, ACCESS_WRITE provides write-through access, and ACCESS_COPY provides copy-on-write access. ACCESS_DEFAULT defers to the prot argument of mmap.

name: ALLOCATIONGRANULARITY
doc: PAGESIZE is the system memory page size in bytes. ALLOCATIONGRANULARITY is the minimum alignment in bytes required for the offset argument of mmap. On Unix, ALLOCATIONGRANULARITY is equal to PAGESIZE.

name: mmap
signatures: mmap(fileno, length, tagname=None, access=ACCESS_DEFAULT, offset=0, *, trackfd=True)
doc:
Windows: mmap(fileno, length[, tagname[, access[, offset[, trackfd]]]])

Maps length bytes from the file specified by the file handle fileno,
and returns a mmap object.  If length is larger than the current size
of the file, the file is extended to contain length bytes.  If length
is 0, the maximum length of the map is the current size of the file,
except that if the file is empty Windows raises an exception (you cannot
create an empty mapping on Windows).

Unix: mmap(fileno, length[, flags[, prot[, access[, offset[, trackfd]]]]])

Maps length bytes from the file specified by the file descriptor fileno,
and returns a mmap object.  If length is 0, the maximum length of the map
will be the current size of the file when mmap is called.
flags specifies the nature of the mapping. MAP_PRIVATE creates a
private copy-on-write mapping, so changes to the contents of the mmap
object will be private to this process, and MAP_SHARED creates a mapping
that's shared with all other processes mapping the same areas of the file.
The default value is MAP_SHARED.

To map anonymous memory, pass -1 as the fileno (both versions).

name: close
doc: Closes the mmap. Subsequent calls to other methods of the object will result in a ValueError exception being raised. This will not close the open file.

name: closed
doc: True if the file is closed.

name: find
doc: Returns the lowest index in the object where the subsequence sub is found, such that sub is contained in the range [start, end]. Optional arguments start and end are interpreted as in slice notation. Returns -1 on failure.

changed.text: Writable bytes-like object is now accepted.

name: flush
doc: Flushes changes made to the in-memory copy of a file back to disk. Without use of this call there is no guarantee that changes are written back before the object is destroyed. If offset and size are specified, only changes to the given range of bytes will be flushed to disk; otherwise, the whole extent of the mapping is flushed. offset must be a multiple of the PAGESIZE or ALLOCATIONGRANULARITY.

changed.text: Previously, a nonzero value was returned on success; zero was returned on error under Windows. A zero value was returned on success; an exception was raised on error under Unix.

Allow specifying offset without size. Previously, both offset and size parameters were required together. Now offset can be specified alone, and the flush operation will extend from offset to the end of the mmap.
Added flags parameter to control synchronization behavior.

name: madvise
doc: Send advice option to the kernel about the memory region beginning at start and extending length bytes. option must be one of the MADV_* constants available on the system. If start and length are omitted, the entire mapping is spanned. On some systems (including Linux), start must be a multiple of the PAGESIZE.

name: move
doc: Copy the count bytes starting at offset src to the destination index dest. If the mmap was created with ACCESS_READ, then calls to move will raise a TypeError exception.

name: read
doc: Return a bytes containing up to n bytes starting from the current file position. If the argument is omitted, None or negative, return all bytes from the current file position to the end of the mapping. The file position is updated to point after the bytes that were returned.

changed.text: Argument can be omitted or None.

name: read_byte
doc: Returns a byte at the current file position as an integer, and advances the file position by 1.

name: readline
doc: Returns a single line, starting at the current file position and up to the next newline. The file position is updated to point after the bytes that were returned.

name: resize
doc: Resizes the map and the underlying file, if any.

changed.text: Correctly fails if attempting to resize when another map is held Allows resize against an anonymous map on Windows

name: rfind
doc: Returns the highest index in the object where the subsequence sub is found, such that sub is contained in the range [start, end]. Optional arguments start and end are interpreted as in slice notation. Returns -1 on failure.

changed.text: Writable bytes-like object is now accepted.

name: seek
doc: Set the file’s current position. whence argument is optional and defaults to os.SEEK_SET or 0 (absolute file positioning); other values are os.SEEK_CUR or 1 (seek relative to the current position) and os.SEEK_END or 2 (seek relative to the file’s end).

changed.text: Return the new absolute position instead of None.

name: seekable
doc: Return whether the file supports seeking, and the return value is always True.

name: set_name
doc: Annotate the memory mapping with the given name for easier identification in /proc/<pid>/maps if the kernel supports the feature and -X dev is passed to Python or if Python is built in debug mode. The length of name must not exceed 67 bytes including the '\0' terminator.

name: size
doc: Return the length of the file, which can be larger than the size of the memory-mapped area. For an anonymous mapping, return its size.

changed.text: Anonymous mappings are now supported on Unix.

name: tell
doc: Returns the current position of the file pointer.

name: write
doc: Write the bytes in bytes into memory at the current position of the file pointer and return the number of bytes written (never less than len(bytes), since if the write fails, a ValueError will be raised). The file position is updated to point after the bytes that were written. If the mmap was created with ACCESS_READ, then writing to it will raise a TypeError exception.

changed.text: Writable bytes-like object is now accepted.
The number of bytes written is now returned.

name: write_byte
doc: Write the integer byte into memory at the current position of the file pointer; the file position is advanced by 1. If the mmap was created with ACCESS_READ, then writing to it will raise a TypeError exception.

name: MS_ASYNC
doc: These flags control the synchronization behavior for mmap.flush():

name: MS_INVALIDATE
doc: These flags control the synchronization behavior for mmap.flush():

name: MS_SYNC
doc: These flags control the synchronization behavior for mmap.flush():

name: PAGESIZE
doc: PAGESIZE is the system memory page size in bytes. ALLOCATIONGRANULARITY is the minimum alignment in bytes required for the offset argument of mmap. On Unix, ALLOCATIONGRANULARITY is equal to PAGESIZE.

name: PROT_EXEC
doc: Memory protection flags accepted by the prot argument of mmap. PROT_READ allows pages to be read, PROT_WRITE allows pages to be written, and PROT_EXEC allows pages to be executed. Values can be combined using the bitwise OR operator. Not every option is present on every system.

name: PROT_READ
doc: Memory protection flags accepted by the prot argument of mmap. PROT_READ allows pages to be read, PROT_WRITE allows pages to be written, and PROT_EXEC allows pages to be executed. Values can be combined using the bitwise OR operator. Not every option is present on every system.

doc: Memory protection flags accepted by the prot argument of mmap. PROT_READ allows pages to be read, PROT_WRITE allows pages to be written, and PROT_EXEC allows pages to be executed. Values can be combined using the bitwise OR operator. Not every option is present on every system.
